messages:
maria: WIP PR up — permissive schema shim for funcall/tool outputs across Go + Ruby SDKs. It tries to treat `null` and missing the same and lets unknown fields through for now. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 :eyes:

ajay: Looking. Quick q: how does this interact with streaming funcall payloads? we sometimes get partial JSON frames and the shim might mis-parse.

maria: Good point. Current plan is simple buffering until we detect a complete top-level JSON value (balance braces/brackets). Hacky but low-risk for non-high-throughput paths.

samira: Brace counting is fragile with strings/escaped braces. Can we instead switch the runtime to emit newline-delimited JSON objects for funcall events? That would make streaming parsers trivial.

maria: Runtime change is possible but touches a lot. This shim is intended as a short-term client-side resilience layer so we don't block rollout.

leo: Also think about arrays from tools — e.g., tool returns `[]` vs `null` vs omitted. Our consumers expect empty list, not null. Are you mapping `null -> []` in the shim?

maria: I added per-schema hints: for fields annotated as list, null -> [] ; for optional scalar fields null->missing. It's configurable per-field. Example helper in Go in the PR:```go
// PermissiveDecode reads possibly-incomplete streams and coalesces null->missing for lists
func PermissiveDecode(b []byte, out interface{}) error {
  var tmp map["string"]json.RawMessage
  if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &tmp); err != nil {
    return err
  }
  // apply per-field rules here
  return json.Unmarshal(b, out)
}
```

ajay: Hmm ok. Two concerns: 1) buffering large responses could OOM, 2) auth retry can re-open stream and we might get half of previous message + new leading data. Any de-dupe or resumable framing?

maria: For (1) we cap buffer at 1MB and fall back to a strict decoder error for extremely large single values. For (2) we added a small stream-id header; client discards partial buffer when it sees a new stream-id on reconnect. Patch in PR.

samira: CI shows some flaky tests in Go streaming tests — devex-bot just reported failures.

devex-bot: CI: go-integration-tests failed on 3 tests (streaming_toolcall_test.go:45, 92, 118). See https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/842/567 for logs.

leo: I'll take a look at the failing test that reproduces the bracket-in-string case. Could be our naive brace-counting when strings contain `{\"` sequences.

maria: Thanks. If you find a simple parser we can vendor (ndjson or eventsource style), I'd prefer that over custom brace counting.

ajay: One more tiny SDK concern: Ruby's JSON parser allows symbolized keys and will happily convert unknown fields — good for permissive mode — but we need parity tests so behavior is consistent across languages. Add crosslang tests in the PR checklist.

maria: Yep, adding crosslang matrix. Plan: split into two PRs — (A) client-side permissive shim + parity tests, (B) streaming framing/stream-id changes in the runtime and clients. Will file (B) after tests from (A) stabilize.

samira: Sounds good. @leo can you prioritize the bracket-in-string fix? If you push a small test + fix to the PR I can re-run CI.

leo: On it, aiming to push in ~30m.

maria: Thanks all — leaving some review comments on the PR now. If anyone objects to the null->list mapping, shout here. Otherwise I'll merge once CI is green and we have a Go + Ruby parity check. :thumbsup:
